fix_commit_message:
avcodec/exr: fix AVERROR typo

Fixes: out of array read
Fixes: 485866440/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_AV_CODEC_ID_EXR_DEC_fuzzer-4520520419966976

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 7e10579f4992 on top of intro 6e8cf0377fee via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (LogicError): In the FFmpeg EXR decoder's decode_header() function, a newly added channel-combination validation branch (added to detect 'uncommon' channel layouts not supported by the decoder) incorrectly double-negates the AVERROR_PATCHWELCOME error constant by writing `AVERROR(AVERROR_PATCHWELCOME)` instead of `AVERROR_PATCHWELCOME`. Since AVERROR_PATCHWELCOME is already a negative FFmpeg error tag, applying the AVERROR() negation macro to it flips the sign, producing a positive value. This causes the error-detection logic (`if (ret < 0) ...`) used throughout the EXR decoder's header parsing and its callers to fail to recognize this specific failure path as an error, allowing decoding to proceed on an EXR file with an unsupported/invalid channel combination. Continuing to process such malformed header data results in an out-of-bounds read later in the decoder, as found by the OSS-Fuzz fuzzer. Root cause: A newly written error-handling branch mistakenly wrapped an already-negative AVERROR_* constant in the AVERROR() negation macro, flipping its sign to positive and thereby defeating the standard `ret < 0` failure-detection convention used elsewhere in the codebase.
